Blood as Nourishment (Rong)

Nourishment (Rong) is the essential qi of water and grain. It harmonizes within the five viscera and spreads throughout the six bowels, and thus can enter the vessels. It is transformed into blood to nourish the four extremities, and internally flows into the five viscera and six bowels, corresponding to the measured intervals. This blood is formed in the middle burner, receiving qi from water and grain, and is transformed to become red — this is what is called the pathway. It then enters the vessels, carrying the essence.

Qi moves and internally connects the network vessels; the upper part governs blood so that the eyes can see and the feet can grasp. When one lies down, blood returns to the liver. When the liver receives blood, it can see. When the feet receive blood, they can walk. When the palms receive blood, they can grasp. When the fingers receive blood, they can hold. When the eyes receive blood, they can see.

The liver spreads and distributes [blood], day by day sending out essence, nourishing and irrigating [the body], so that blood enables sight, the feet enable movement, and the hands enable grasping.

When yin grows, it draws out fluid and transforms it, turning red to become blood — this is the constant principle. Therefore, when one eats food and blood is abundant, the body is robust; when blood is weak, the body declines. Yang infuses [the body] and thus blood is generated.

Blood is paired with Qi

When [qi] is weak and declining, the physical form [suffers].

Qi stops circulation, blood stops; when qi is warm, it covers like water; qi is the commander of blood, like wind directing wood — when qi moves, blood moves above, where qi goes blood follows.

Governing [the body] means guiding circulation; reaching the upper [regions], regulating what is there; qi and breath then cause the blood's area to flow smoothly; in illness and cold, blood and dampness regulate qi — within one breath it can be assessed throughout the whole body.

Pulse Methods

In blood loss, all pulse [presentations] seen daily — the pulse obtaining various [qualities], the prized [pulse] being sunken, thin, floating — [these] are difficult to treat. The Pulse Essentials says: in all such patterns, throughout the body, one may assess [them].

When heat [causes] blood loss, if at the time of vomiting the pulse arrives and the blood loss stops — again, the Lingshu says: in vomiting blood, the pulse must stop. In great blood loss, the Essentials says: in all such patterns...

In major channels: when the pulse is large and one is vomiting, [if] the pulse arrives at that point, it is difficult [to treat]; in severe illness the patient dies. Again, vomiting with an abdominal distension, thin pulse, loose bowels, and contradictory pulse [signs].

[When] floating [pulse], as in the Han [formula], with large [pulse] and vomiting arriving with blood — [this is] hard to resolve; in severe illness, if the patient dies; with vomiting and replete, full blood, [the condition] is difficult to treat; [pulse that is] small and weak...

Blood [conditions with] full, replete, large pulse — those [patients] die; among various [cases], with rapid pulse it is difficult to treat; with vomiting and replete blood it is difficult to treat; small and weak [pulse]...

Heat Can Injure Blood

Heat can injure blood; the heart [rules] the nine [openings]; heat and blazing cannot be remedied; the heart stir-fries [i.e., overheats]; when heat is extreme, heat injures blood; blood exits from the heart, [the patient] feels faint and wishes to cleanse [the body].

Seven Emotions Stirring Blood

It is said that one must understand yin, yet one cannot do without it. This is what Danxi (Zhu Danxi, the Yuan dynasty physician) said: "All blood disorders arise from heat; when blood is seen, it is always a heat pattern." When yang is excess and yin is deficient, the blood fails to return to the channels. He also said: when yang is exuberant and yin is deficient, there is excess above and deficiency below — supplementing the yang excess. Hence, fresh bright-red blood that is warm flows freely; blood that encounters cold congeals and becomes sluggish; pale blood comes from the channels; dark black blood is softened and issues upward from the nose and mouth — the method of enriching blood fully supplements yang exuberance. In one phrase it may be summed up. Yet it cannot be summed up in one phrase alone.

To know the essentials, one phrase suffices to encompass all. Yet one cannot do without it. When the qi rebels upward, blood overflows out of the mouth and nose — the method of enriching blood supplements yang exuberance.

When blood stirs, it overflows and causes vomiting of blood. When anger causes qi to rebel upward, blood rushes upward, making people violently agitated in the heart. Anger then causes the qi to be extreme.

When blood overflows through the nose, anger causes qi rebellion; blood rushes upward, causing violent agitation of the heart. Suppressing the teacher/guide, the qi becomes extreme.

For disorders of yin, it is appropriate to use the Baoming Shengdi Xuanhuang Tu Powder (Life-Preserving Rehmannia-Coptis-Earth Formula) for fire damaging the blood internally — the seven emotions injure and cause agitation.

Excessive thought and worry injures the heart and spleen, impairing the generation of blood; sudden dispersion stirs the liver.

Joy and heat injure the liver; the spleen loses control; the kidneys and all are linked — suddenly the liver is stirred.

This blood of the liver — anger causes spontaneous recovery; vomiting of blood suddenly; injury to the liver; the formula Lian Ming San with Qingdai (indigo), Wuhu (five tiger ingredients), Dagan Cao (licorice) — calming and soothing.

Its liver is without fault — both sides suffer sudden violence; the heart then causes qi to shift, moving with licorice.

Blood in the urine without cause comes from the liver; from great exertion and overwork, the channels become disrupted, leading to disorder of yin; thus the liver fails to contain the blood.

Internal Injury and Blood Loss

Various Syndromes of Blood Loss

When there is overflow and excess, suddenly and acutely, overeating and drinking causes the vessels to become full; irregular daily activities and overexertion externally —

When there is surplus, blood exits from the seven yang collaterals, injuring the blood vessels; yang collaterals injured cause blood to overflow internally; afterward the vessels fill with blood and overflow externally.

When blood seeps and percolates through, it enters the intestines; taxation causes blood loss; various syndromes arise below, with blood moving downward through the bowels and urine, accumulating in the large and small intestines, causing vomiting; the bladder causes bloody stool; blood overflows internally, leading to blood deficiency.

Phlegm and stasis, dark yellow, stagnant and blocked; heat rises, transforming yin; when deficient yang accumulates as redness, great yang causes large and small bowel bleeding in the urine.

Colors: pain, itching, heat on the skin; when yang and yin are extreme, there is decay; deficient yang accumulates, causing vomiting; when the organ is overwhelmed, there is bloody stool; when blood overflows internally, blood deficiency results.

Green-tinted blood originates from the stomach, entering upward; it may arise from the mouth, the nose, or the skin; daily it transforms into dark phlegm; blood rises upward; the person likes to hemorrhage; water diarrhea opens externally; then heat consumes the blood.

Blood issuing from below comes from the lungs, or from the blood itself; vomiting of blood rises upward from the nose; what is called blood-streaked throat.

Blood exits following the lung; it may come from the large intestine; blood coming from the lungs arrives with vomiting; it exits through the throat as blood-streaked phlegm.

Blood exits through sweat pores; blood comes from the muscles; blood comes from the root of the teeth; blood comes from the intestinal wind; in the small intestine, phlegm carries blood; from the root of the tongue, blood is regulated.

Nine types arise from coughing; the tongue has blood in all cases; examining the color of new and old blood; blood is regulated from within; nine types of blood exit; from regulating the blood and pulse, blood exits from the diaphragm; blood exits from regulation.

Distinguishing New and Old Blood by Color

Black color — summer-heat syndrome. Red color — old blood. Red rinse — black color. Also resembling smoke and soot — a smoke-soot syndrome. Clear water color — cold syndrome.

Accumulated Blood (蓄血)

Symptoms and Signs: In yang-type excess patterns, there is repeated passage of fresh bright blood. In yin-type patterns, as the condition worsens, the stool resembles the color of liver tissue, initially brownish in color.

When there is mania, blood accumulation, forgetfulness, and suppressed fire causing dryness and scorching, the condition resembles sheep's blood stagnation; on that very day the color turns dark, and the stool becomes brownish.

With accumulated blood mixed with yellow and black hues, there is frequent urination; as the disease progresses, blood accumulates, and there is injury to the small intestine; with cold-heat alternation, the disease manifests with dark urine resembling that pattern.

Below: the patient cries out, the illness manifests day and night, the stool is heavy, thirst persists, and blood accumulates; the small intestine is affected; frequent urination with no desire to drink water; in milder cases it resembles mania with dark urine.

Upper and middle: scorching in the upper burner; the affected region shows good signs of blood; mild epidemic-like confusion; small frequent urination with no desire; the condition resembles mania with dark urine.

When feces become dry and hard in the lower abdomen, with hardness and pain, Tao Ren Cheng Qi Tang (Peach Pit Order-Resolving Decoction) is appropriate to prevent blood stagnation in the middle and lower burners.

For dryness and binding, use Sheng Di, Yu Huang, Da Gan Cao, Jian Tao Ren to break up stagnant blood. Tao Ren in all cases breaks up stagnant blood. Ginger and Tribulus are also used.

For blood accumulation in the lower burner, use wood-based and spirit-strengthening herbs including Wu Huang, Da Gan Cao, and Jian Tao Ren to expel the accumulation. For accumulated blood in the lower burner, ginger and Tribulus are used.韭 (chive) juice, Ling Dan, and other herbs combined with Wu Huang, Da Gan Cao, Ling Dan, Fu Tao Ren all break up stagnant blood.

Saengjiwhang-tang (Fresh Rehmannia Decoction)

Use half a liang of fresh Rehmannia; pound it cold, press out one large sheng of juice. [Indicated for] blood-pattern disorders with black [discoloration], small sunken thin faint pulse, and [conditions affecting] the gallbladder and qi; especially suitable for those who are weak, and also for those who are delirious or agitated.

[Ingredients include:] ten leaves, one piece of stir-fried [ingredient], one sheng, half a sheng of juice, half a sheng — use dried peach kernel, half a sheng ground, two liang stir-fried, ten parts water, ten sheng, stir-fried together with water, lightly dry-fried.

Compare this prescription with the carp soup — test against each other in cold [constitution]. Take in two portions of nine [doses]; first take a small amount, fearing [adverse effects]; when the time comes, allow nine portions; when blood in the stool fails to stop after three sheng of water, stop again and decoct again.

Prognostic Signs in Blood Disorders

When [the condition is] severe and the patient cannot bear heat, [the patient] will die quickly; when the pulse flows smoothly, recovery is easy. When [there is] no tidal fever and the blood discharge is light with heat in the body and tidal [fever], [prognosis is good].

When [the condition involves] vigorous lung [qi] and the pulse is full, it will break up the blood; if the form is like [boiling] heat surging upward with flushed complexion, large [open] mouth and nose, white [pallor] appearing — if this occurs afterward and downward bleeding is treated, recovery is possible; if blood is excessive and the heart and lower [burner] are hot, this is severe.

When the pulse is small and rapid, this indicates [pathology in] the flesh and membranes. If the pulse is small and forceful yet stops moving, and there is blood in the stool with abdominal fullness, pain radiating to the back and abdomen — this is serious.

When downward movement occurs again and the condition transforms into festering and counterflow, with the flesh and membranes separating and the pulse becoming thin — this is a counterflow pulse. [This is among the] critical [signs].

Loss of Blood and Collapse of Blood: Signs and Symptoms

When blood loss is accompanied by fever, the condition is easy to treat. When the pulse is large, it is difficult to treat. When treatment is said to be difficult, it means evil qi is dominant. When it is said to be easy to treat, it means blood is seeping upward, or the pulse is cool or calm.

In cases of bleeding downward: if there is vomiting, treatment below is difficult. If it flows naturally without symptoms, following the normal course, and then descends, treatment is easy. If suddenly the flow changes, this is what Zhongjing calls blood accumulation rising upward, or the body becomes cool and the pulse calm.

When descending: currently, blood will heal on its own. If it moves upward without signs, then suddenly the person's flow changes — this is what Zhongjing refers to as accumulation, rising upward.

Regarding heat — if one cannot determine whether the prognosis is good or bad, the person dies. Zhongjing said: observe this blood — if the disease worsens, if blood and qi are named in the pulse, then evil and disease are manifested.

Regarding the Sea of Blood: if the head is not well, color is white, the body is deficient in blood. Furthermore, if the Chong vessel loses its vital essence, the face appears without luster.

Li Dongyuan said: if the pulse is thin and rough, and the body is not at ease, then the body's pulse is full but vacuous and hollow inside. [The formulas follow.]

Nosebleed connects to the brain blood. When blood comes out of both the mouth and nose together, this benefits the brain blood, which exits through the nose by way of the Yangming channel.

The Three Yellow Formula, Sichuan Xiong Powder, and Blood-Nourishing and Blood-Clearing Decoctions using chicken and garlic can resolve and disperse. It is also said that brain blood exits through the nose, which disperses through the Yangming channel.

For nourishing blood: use Dihuang (rehmannia), Danshen, and promote blood circulation. Preserve life by generating blood with Shaoyao (peony) to cool the earth.

Regarding the pathway of blood flow: the main position is governed by the angle of Dihuang Decoction — enter through Mamen, use hemp, gold, and tablets, decoct and raise medicinals, scatter and generate.

Sichuan Xiong Powder: Treats nosebleed. Xiangfu (cyperus) decocted as tea, adjusted with Xiangfu, used at the four seasons, two liang of Chuanxiong, two liang of Hanxin method, ground into powder, taken each time — one dose.

If not taken at the right time: refer to Danxi's Heart Method for harmonizing blood. Same formula.

Tonifying: Xiangfu opens the orifices, moves qi, causes the blood's six pulses to become deficient while internal fire flares up; vomiting blood — use Shengma, Baishao, and Banxia/Dongchong, each seven fen.

Three Yellow Blood-Supplementing Decoction: Treats [nosebleed]. Dihuang one qian, Danggui, Chuanxiong, each seven fen.

When injury does not produce nosebleed, the blood turns purple and becomes stagnant. It is also said: Xiangfu and Yangming — also said: the Ā formula in spring benefits those types of patients. The body is hot; also, use Mahuang formulas with vomiting blood. Method: the Yin and Spleen move to heat, and life is generated.

Methods to Stop Nosebleed

For treating nosebleeds that have persisted for a long time and have not responded to various medicines: Take a large sheet of white paper, soak it in cold water, and place it on top of the head — this stops nosebleeds immediately. If still not stopped, roll paper into plugs and insert into both nostrils; the bleeding will stop. If still not stopped, and blood is coming from both nostrils, apply crushed garlic (one clove, peeled and ground into a paste like a cake) to the Yongquan acupoint (Kidney 1): if the left nostril bleeds, apply to the right foot; if the right nostril bleeds, apply to the left foot. Take the formula in water. Formula: equal parts of Sanleng (sparganium) and Maidong (ophiopogon), grind into powder, mix with cold water, apply to the nose for bleeding that will not stop.

Dispersing method for treating severe nosebleeds that will not stop: Take half a sheet of paper, fold into two pieces, twist into ten paper rolls, plug both nostrils — bleeding stops at once. Or plug the middle of both nostrils; oral bleeding stops immediately.

Medicines: Green vitriol (green alum) — apply to stop nosebleed from the right nostril; blood stops.

Vomiting Blood and Spitting Blood

Soup (decoction) stimulating the lungs, with Sophora flower, connecting the stomach internally — for cases where vomiting blood occurs with hiccup sounds, use Qianjin (Thousand Gold) Banxia Dihuang Tang (Decoction); for deficiency cases with small irregularities.

For nosebleed where blood has seeped from the pores: the blood is suspected to come from between the heart and lungs, flowing into the stomach and then vomited. It may appear in amounts like beans, or as much as ginger-sized pieces. After drinking alcohol, at the time of vomiting, blood comes out from the lungs after vomiting, sometimes in amounts of one he (合) or more, sometimes mixed with spirits.

Distinguishing Yin and Yang, Deficiency and Excess in Sleep

In sleep excess, the patient belongs to Yang — the original qi is abundant and the sleep is full. One who sleeps facing the wall in stillness has deficiency of original qi and damage to external qi. When qi descends downward, the yang pathway is obstructed and cannot follow its proper course. Therefore one cannot properly recline. Body Heaviness and Drowsiness

Thus, when qi lingers in the yang, the yang qi is exhausted and moves into the yin; when the yin qi is exhausted, the eyes close in sleep. Therefore, excessive sleeping occurs.
